items.titleEn: Why is Baidu stock crashing to a five-year low despite 94% AI cloud growth?
items.summaryEn: Buy Baidu HK$9888. The market is pricing the 22% ad slump as if AI cloud is failing, but cloud revenue +94% and GPU cloud +191% show real demand. Cloud economics are improving (infra profit/margin up yoy and qoq) and longer contracts/prepayments add visibility. The stock is at a five-year low, giving a better entry before monetization catches up. Key Risk: Advertising keeps shrinking and AI-native ads keep falling (no rebound in core monetization), forcing more dilution/financing needs. Buy Alibaba HK$9988 as a relative winner. Baidu’s thesis is “AI cloud grows but ads lag.” Alibaba is better positioned to monetize AI across its ecosystem and has more diversified revenue streams, so it’s less dependent on a single ad recovery. If China ad budgets stay cautious, the market will rotate toward platforms with steadier cash flow and monetization power.

items.titleEn: Samsung and SK Hynix stocks sink as a 20% chip price shock hits home
items.summaryEn: Buy Samsung Electronics (005660.KS). Samsung is more diversified across AI memory customers (Google/AMD and others) and has a clearer path to regain HBM competitiveness as Nvidia share of shipments shifts. The article notes DRAM price increases are still forecast and Samsung reported strong memory facility utilization through September. If the market is over-discounting a NAND spot move, Samsung’s mix shift toward higher-value AI memory should cushion the downside and let the stock rebound faster than SK Hynix. Key Risk: NAND contract prices fall faster than expected and the AI mix shift doesn’t offset the margin hit. Sell SK Hynix (005930.KS). The news shows a 20% NAND spot price shock and management can’t hide that it’s hitting conventional NAND first, with smartphone/PC demand rolling over. Even if AI DRAM/HBM holds, SK Hynix’s near-term earnings sensitivity is higher because it’s more tied to Nvidia-driven HBM order timing while NAND is already repricing. The stock is already down hard—this is the next leg: contract pricing weakness spreading earlier than expected.

items.titleEn: PayPal Tracks $53 Billion in Treasury Cash With an AI Agent
items.summaryEn: PayPal deployed a conversational AI agent in treasury operations covering $53 billion in funds, allowing employees to analyze cash positions, currency exposure and financial risks through natural-language queries. PayPal’s broader treasury overhaul eliminated 90 spreadsheets, saved about 1,700 hours and increased cash visibility from 78% to nearly 100% across roughly 1,000 accounts. Generative AI use for cash flow management rose from 16% to 80% of finance teams, PYMNTS Intelligence found, but only 5% use agentic AI for cash flow management.

items.titleEn: Gold, silver extend losses as tech selloff, dollar pressure metals- Kitco PM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold and silver prices were lower in late U.S. trading Monday, extending last week's sharp losses as a firmer dollar, expectations for additional Federal Reserve tightening and a broad technology-led equity selloff pressured precious metals. Gold struggled to hold the $3,850.00 level as investors reduced exposure to risk assets, while silver suffered heavier selling amid concerns about industrial demand and tighter financial conditions. Gold was trading near $3,855.50 an ounce, down $27.90, or 0.72%, while silver was trading near $46.860, down $1.771, or 3.64%, on the session. Gold traded as low as $3,832.20 during the day, while silver touched $46.430. Monday's U.S. economic data showed a sharp slowdown in New York manufacturing activity, although the sector continued expanding. The Federal Reserve Bank of New York's November Empire State manufacturing index declined to 7.8 from 25.5 in October, substantially below expectations near 17.6. New orders and shipments continued increasing, while employment expanded at its fastest pace in more than four years. Input and selling price increases moderated but remained elevated. The report followed Friday's October producer price index, which increased 0.3% on the month, below expectations, while annual producer inflation reached 6.5%, its highest level since November 2022. The combination of slowing regional manufacturing growth and persistent inflation highlights the difficulties facing the Fed as it considers further monetary tightening.

items.titleEn: Is Robinhood stock a buy after the crypto crash and new Kalshi competition fears?
items.summaryEn: Buy a public exchange/brokerage proxy that benefits from more retail trading activity tied to prediction/derivatives platforms—buy Interactive Brokers Group (IBKR). If Kalshi’s perpetual stock futures and broader stock trading pull more retail volume into “trading platforms,” IBKR’s customer trading and execution ecosystem tends to capture incremental activity across venues. This is a volume/engagement tailwind, not a HOOD-specific bet. Key Risk: Regulators clamp down on prediction/derivatives-style products or retail trading growth slows, reducing incremental volumes that would flow to IBKR. Sell Robinhood (HOOD). The stock is in a confirmed technical downtrend (death cross, below 61.8% retracement) and fundamentals are pressured by crypto weakness (crypto volumes down, crypto revenue falling). Add Kalshi’s stock-trading expansion: it’s stealing the same “trading for retail” attention and flow HOOD needs to stabilize revenue. Target $60; cover if HOOD reclaims $80.

items.titleEn: Tesla stock falls 2.5% even as company plans $3.3B cybercab expansion
items.summaryEn: Buy TSLA. The €3.3B German Cybercab expansion is a concrete step toward scaling robotaxi production outside Texas, which should improve unit economics and reduce delivery bottlenecks. Customer Cybercab sales plus a subscription validate demand for Tesla’s “physical AI” stack, and JPMorgan’s shift to more constructive supports upside optionality. Key Risk: Cybercab production slips materially (permits, construction, or ramp), so Tesla can’t scale robotaxi revenue on the timeline investors are pricing. Sell European EV component/auto suppliers most exposed to slow EV demand and margin pressure (e.g., Continental AG, Valeo, Schaeffler). If Tesla’s scaled Cybercab manufacturing strengthens in Germany, it can pull share and talent from traditional EV programs, while Europe’s sluggish demand and Chinese price pressure keep margins under stress.

items.titleEn: Walmart's Low-Price Retail Strategy Faces a Profit Test This Earnings
items.summaryEn: Walmart has spent years making low prices its competitive advantage. Now, it faces the more complicated test of proving that the customers attracted by those prices are worth more to the business. Δ document.getElementById( "ak_js_1" ).setAttribute( "value", ( new Date() ).getTime() ); When the retail giant reports fiscal third-quarter earnings this Thursday (Nov. 19), investors will be looking beyond comparable sales and holiday forecasts for evidence that Walmart’s expanding digital ecosystem can convert customer traffic into higher-margin revenue. Walmart’s opportunity is to make money from more than the products customers put in their carts.
